response.sql:
WITH patient_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(HGB / HCT) as ratio
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) as avg_ratio
  FROM patient_ratios
),
above_overall AS (
  SELECT 
    pr.ratio,
    (pr.ratio - oa.avg_ratio) as above_overall_avg
  FROM patient_ratios pr
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
  WHERE pr.ratio > oa.avg_ratio
),
group_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) as avg_ratio
  FROM above_overall
),
final_group AS (
  SELECT 
    ao.ratio,
    ao.above_overall_avg,
    (ao.ratio - ga.avg_ratio) as above_group_avg
  FROM above_overall ao
  CROSS JOIN group_avg ga
  WHERE ao.ratio > ga.avg_ratio
)
SELECT 
  AVG(ratio) as avg_ratio,
  AVG(above_overall_avg) as avg_above_overall,
  AVG(above_group_avg) as avg_above_group
FROM final_group

assumptions.assumption: Each patient's ratio is calculated by averaging HGB/HCT across all their lab records—one aggregated ratio per patient. The phrase 'each patient's ratio' (singular) and 'keep the patients' suggest per-patient aggregation rather than treating individual test records separately.

alternatives.interpretation: Each lab record (each date-stamped test) represents a separate ratio instance. Patients with multiple tests contribute multiple ratio values to the analysis.
